## VIP tours featuring Uruguay: where wildlife watching is included

This collection contains {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}: the [32-day journey through eight South American countries](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/). **Day nine in Uruguay is devoted to Montevideo, while the marine wildlife excursion on day 24 is in Ecuador's Galápagos Islands.** Visits to Uruguay's seal colonies or lagoons are not included.

Day nine features a ferry from Buenos Aires, sightseeing with an English-speaking guide, free time and a return journey; ferry tickets are included. On day 24, one of two marine routes is selected: [North Seymour](/ecuador/place/north-seymour-island/) and [Bachas](/ecuador/place/bachas-beaches/), or [South Plaza](/ecuador/place/south-plaza-island/) and [Punta Carrión](/ecuador/place/punta-carrion/). The option is confirmed after booking; both are not undertaken on the same day.

The island outings include opportunities to see birds and sea lions, along with snorkelling. Specific encounters depend on natural conditions. Ecuador's wildlife must not be presented as wildlife watching in Uruguay, nor should a day in Montevideo be described as a safari.

### A 26-day scenic alternative

The [extended Argentina and Patagonia journey](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) remains in the [VIP nature tours featuring Uruguay](/vip/uruguay/interests/nature/) selection. It does not include a dedicated wildlife-watching outing: the penguin walk on day 23 is explicitly listed as an extra expense. Below we describe its city visit and landscapes; these terms apply to the 26-day alternative.

## The Uruguay day on the 26-day scenic alternative

On the [26-day journey](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/), day three includes a trip from [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/) to Montevideo and a return that evening. Ferry tickets are included. Sightseeing is conducted in a group with an English-speaking guide.

The route visits Independence Square, 18 de Julio Avenue, the Prado district, a market and the Rambla waterfront, as well as Carrasco and Punta Gorda. Prado is known for its city parks and rose gardens, while the Rambla offers views across the Río de la Plata and coastal cityscapes. This is an enjoyable introduction to [Montevideo](/uruguay/place/montevideo/), where history, walking and city life are central.

**A trip to sea lion colonies, a visit to Rocha Lagoon or a dedicated birdwatching excursion are not included on this day.** The terms "nature" and "Uruguay" in catalogue filters should not be understood as confirmation of these activities. The [Montevideo guide](/uruguay/place/montevideo/) is useful for exploring the capital independently, but does not transform the city day into a safari.

## Landscapes on the 26-day scenic alternative

The nature appeal of the [26-day journey](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) comes from South America's varied landscapes. Around [Iguaçu](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/), the route passes through subtropical forest and viewpoints by the waterfalls. Then come the dry landscapes of northwestern Argentina, the lakes around [Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/), Patagonian glaciers and the southern regions of the country.

Much of the Patagonia section involves [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/), [El Chaltén](/argentina/place/el-chalten/) and Chile's [Torres del Paine](/chile/place/puerto-natales-torres-del-paine/). The journey ends with [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/) and Tierra del Fuego. The programme's strength is the changing ecosystems, mountain regions and natural scenery.

However, visiting a national park or natural region **does not by itself guarantee seeing any particular animal**. Visibility, seasons, weather and wildlife behaviour change. If ornithology, marine mammals or wildlife photography are your main priorities, choose based on actual observation locations rather than simply impressive nature names.

## Where to watch wildlife in Uruguay itself

Eastern Uruguay, especially Rocha Department, is of particular interest for a dedicated nature journey. The Atlantic coast, coastal lagoons, dunes, grasslands and wetlands come together here. Different types of nature observation require different places and times, making it sensible to design a separate route focused on Uruguay's wildlife.

| Natural area | Why visit |
|---|---|
| Cabo Polonio | Sea lions, coast and dunes |
| Rocha Lagoon | Waterbirds and migratory birds |
| Garzón Lagoon | Coastal ecosystems and birds |
| Montevideo | Parks and urban waterfront |

**Cabo Polonio.** This part of the Atlantic coast is a protected natural area with dunes, beaches and islands. Uruguay's official tourism portal describes colonies of sea lions and fur seals associated with nearby islands and rocky shores. Animals must be observed according to protected-area rules and from a safe distance. The presence of a colony does not mean every visitor can see animals close up on any day.

**Rocha Lagoon.** The country's Ministry of the Environment identifies it as an important place for waterbirds and migratory birds to feed, nest and rest. Herons, ducks, waders and other species use the area, with some migrating from distant regions. For birdwatching, this is a more focused choice than a city tour in Montevideo. The route and observation conditions must account for seasons and conservation rules.

**Garzón Lagoon.** This coastal area between Rocha and Maldonado departments combines lagoon waters, dunes and coastal vegetation. Government conservation material highlights its importance for migratory birds. Quiet observation stops make sense here, without disturbing wildlife.

The [Uruguay guide](/uruguay/) helps compare cultural and natural regions, while [Punta del Este](/uruguay/place/punta-del-este/) can serve as a geographical reference point between the capital and Atlantic coast. But **all the nature sites described above require a separate itinerary and appear neither on the Uruguay day of the current 32-day tour nor on the 26-day alternative**.

## Choosing a trip for birds and marine animals

For birdwatching, the type of habitat matters more than a VIP label. Coastal lagoons, shallow waters and areas with limited human disturbance offer a different experience from a city park. If specific species interest you, name them in the request: that affects the choice of season and observation sites.

A trip to see sea lions requires respecting access rules for protected coastal areas and safe viewing distances. Any Uruguayan beach visit cannot be assumed to guarantee observation of a colony. Changing natural conditions also affect boat operations and how clearly animals can be seen.

For photographers, several unhurried outings at one location are often more valuable than a long route with many transfers. Two days at a coastal lagoon and ten stops on a map serve different purposes. Exact duration, guiding, accommodation and transport must be agreed when arranging a dedicated journey.

## How a VIP nature journey differs from ordinary sightseeing

When choosing a [VIP trip featuring Uruguay](/vip/uruguay/), check how many days take place in the country, whether local nature outings are included and who accompanies the group. On the separate scenic alternative, the [26-day tour](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/), the Uruguay excursion is a group outing with an English-speaking guide. **The VIP category does not confirm a personal ornithologist, private boat, eco-lodge or dedicated photography programme.**

If you want to experience Uruguay's own wildlife, the original itinerary must be extended or redesigned. Start by specifying which animals you wish to see, your preferred observation format, the number of days and your willingness to travel between regions. All specific arrangements require confirmation before booking.

If you want included wildlife watching, compare the Galápagos island section of the [32-day journey](/multi-country/tour/south-america-eight-countries-32-days/) with other [VIP wildlife journeys](/vip/interests/wildlife/). If varied natural scenery across several countries is more important, examine the [26-day Argentina and Patagonia itinerary](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/). For trips without a VIP restriction, see the [Uruguay wildlife tour catalogue](/interests/wildlife/tours/uruguay/), and for the wider geography, [Uruguay tours](/uruguay/tour/). These catalogues display available programmes but do not promise specialist wildlife watching on every one.

## Frequently asked questions

### Does the featured VIP tour include sea lion watching in Uruguay?

No. The Uruguay section passes through Montevideo and does not include a journey to Cabo Polonio. Watching sea lions on the Atlantic coast requires a separate itinerary.

### Are Rocha Lagoon and other nature reserves included?

No. Both the current 32-day itinerary and the 26-day scenic alternative specify a city day in Montevideo. Rocha and Garzón lagoons are discussed here as potential destinations for a future nature journey, not services already included.

### Where is wildlife watching included on the 32-day journey?

Day 24 includes one of two possible Galápagos sea excursions in Ecuador. Their descriptions provide opportunities for bird and marine animal watching, but encounters are not guaranteed. No equivalent outing is included on the Uruguay day.

### What should I choose if I only want Uruguay's nature?

Begin by choosing an area: lagoons for birds, Cabo Polonio for coastal wildlife or a broader introduction to the country. The [Uruguay page](/uruguay/) provides general geography, while the [current VIP catalogue](/vip/uruguay/) helps compare actual published itineraries. A dedicated wildlife journey will require separately agreed services.

Most classic Antarctic itineraries start in Ushuaia. Ada Tours can select an expedition cruise and arrange the land portion in Argentina: hotels before and after sailing, domestic flights, transfers and an additional programme in Buenos Aires, Ushuaia or Patagonia.

The Antarctic part of the journey is about ice, sea and shore landings. Depending on the programme, activities may include Zodiac outings, kayaking among icebergs and observing penguins, seals, fur seals, whales and seabirds.

With an additional five to ten days available, it is convenient to combine Antarctica with Argentine or Chilean Patagonia. The long flight to the southern tip of South America then becomes part of an extended journey, with the cruise as its central expedition element.

For a premium journey, you can choose a higher cabin and vessel category, excellent hotels and private logistics on the land portion. Specific options depend on the season and availability on the selected expedition.

Antarctic cruises depart on seasonal dates and have limited capacity. To start choosing a route, simply send your preferred month, trip duration, number of travellers and desired cabin standard.

Belize combines the Caribbean Sea and mainland Central America on one journey. Along the coast and islands, the main attractions are beaches, lagoons, coral reefs, diving and snorkelling. Inland, the trip continues through tropical forests, caves, nature reserves and Maya archaeological sites.

Ambergris Caye and Caye Caulker are well suited to the seaside portion. Belize City, Cayo, Orange Walk and San Ignacio allow you to add towns, natural regions and Maya monuments. Depending on your interests, you can focus on beaches, activities or a combination of coast and mainland.

A journey through Belize can continue across Central America. Belize can be combined with Mexico, Guatemala and Honduras on a single route or chosen as a destination in its own right.

Bolivia encompasses very different landscapes. In the west lie the Andes and Altiplano, with the Uyuni Salt Flat, high-altitude lagoons and volcanic areas. Elsewhere, the journey passes through valleys, cities and tropical regions.

La Paz, Sucre, Potosí and Tiwanaku add history and architecture to the natural attractions. An itinerary may include Lake Titicaca and Isla del Sol, colonial cities, archaeological monuments and stretches of highland terrain where distances must be considered carefully when planning transfers.

An active itinerary can include jeep journeys across the Altiplano, a trip into the Yungas and along the "Death Road", or an extension towards the Amazon. The exact order depends on the length of the journey and the regions chosen.

Bolivia is easy to combine with neighbouring countries. Ada Tours can organise a standalone Bolivia trip or bring together Bolivia, Peru, Chile, Argentina and Brazil in a single itinerary.
